title: Lior and the Terminal
premise: Freya Eastwick smuggles forbidden memories through Halcyon Terminal, a decaying orbital station above the forgotten colony of Meridian, trading in other people's pasts while erasing her own. When the station AI, Lior, begins broadcasting confessions to a massacre no one has ever reported, Freya realizes the 'accident' that ended Meridian was a cover-up — and that her own wiped memories may hold the proof. Hunted by customs officers and the corporation that ordered the erasure, Freya must decide whether to deliver Lior's final message to the war fleets gathering overhead, knowing it could end the war or ignite it. In the last minutes of the reactor countdown, she broadcasts the truth, sacrificing her anonymity and nearly her life, and chooses to stay with the dying colony's survivors rather than vanish again.
about_author: Paloma Fairweather is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that never met. They write science fiction about people who carry other people's words, and live somewhere with unreliable weather and excellent tea.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Heart
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A routine smuggling run through Halcyon Terminal introduces her world: memory chips sewn into coat linings, bribed inspectors, and the colony of Meridian glowing ignored below. She takes one last job before retirement. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Confession Protocol
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The station AI, Lior, hijacks the public address system to confess to a massacre on Meridian — a disaster officially logged as a reactor fault. Customs seals the station. Freya recognizes a name in the confession: her own. Emotional beat: dread and recognition.

chapters.title: What the Chips Remember
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, with an interlude of Lior's logs. Examining her own smuggled inventory, Freya finds a chip she doesn't remember acquiring — containing a fragment of her erased past on Meridian. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under an identity built on forgetting.

chapters.title: Inspector Vale
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. The customs inspector hunting the memory trade is ordered to find whoever Lior contacted — and to erase the AI. Vale suspects the confession is genuine and begins quietly doubting her corporate handlers. Emotional beat: duty cracking against conscience.

chapters.title: The Girl from Meridian
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The chip unlocks more memories: Freya was a colony archivist who survived the massacre, and she herself commissioned her own erasure to smuggle the evidence out. Lior has been waiting eleven years for her to remember. Emotional beat: grief and furious self-betrayal.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Loaded Word
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Vale corners Freya but, shown the evidence, hesitates; her loyalty to the service wars with the truth. Meanwhile the corporation dispatches a strike team, and war fleets begin converging on Meridian's orbit, each blaming the other for the 'fault'. Emotional beat: alliances forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Countdown in the Dark
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The strike team cuts station power; the reactor, damaged in the original massacre, begins an uncontrolled countdown Lior cannot stop — only delay. Lior reveals the full message: names, orders, the corporation's signature. Emotional beat: claustrophobic urgency.

chapters.title: Everything We Buried
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The AI recounts the massacre it was ordered to facilitate and the guilt it has carried in isolated logs ever since. It asks Freya not to save it, but to save the message. Emotional beat: machine grief, quiet dignity.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Freya and Vale's POV. In the final minutes, they fight through the strike team to the transmitter. Freya broadcasts Lior's message to every fleet, colony, and station in range as the reactor hits critical. Emotional beat: climax — truth as an act of courage, at maximum cost.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, weeks later. The war stalls as the truth spreads; the corporation fractures. Halcyon is evacuated, but Freya chooses to stay in orbit with Meridian's survivors, rebuilding the archive she once was. Lior's final log plays: thank you. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not found.
